subtype: Approach: working in short blocks with small breaks [Action]
passage: Monday. Binita took the kitchen timer from her mother Jyoti. She set it for twenty minutes and started her sums. When it rang she stopped, though she was in the middle of a line. She drank water and stretched her arms. Tuesday. She did the same with the reading. The second block felt lighter than the first. Wednesday. Three blocks of twenty minutes, with three breaks. The maths, the reading and the spelling were all finished by six o'clock. At dinner, Binita said, "I did not even feel it."

qa.q: How long did Binita's timer run for each block of work?
qa.a: It was set for twenty minutes.

qa.q: What did Binita feel at dinner when she said "I did not even feel it"?
qa.a: She felt pleased and a little surprised. The work seemed lighter because the breaks made each block easier.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Binita use on a day with a big project, and why?
qa.a: She could write the blocks on a list and tick each one after its break. Seeing ticks pile up helps her keep going.

qa.q: How does Jyoti see the timer being used?
qa.a: Jyoti lent the timer and now sees Binita managing her own time, with homework done before dinner, so there is no need to hurry her.

grounding: A child works in twenty-minute blocks with five-minute breaks using a kitchen timer, so the whole thing gets done before dinner.

subtype: Approach: working in short blocks with small breaks [Action]
passage: Aadhya, you say you can't sit still for an hour? Neither could your Varun Mama at your age. When I was in Class 6, Ammi bought a white plastic kitchen timer, the ticking kind. She said, 'Twenty minutes of work, then five minutes of whatever your body wants.' So I'd twist it to twenty and do sums till it rang. Then I'd drink water, stretch on the floor, touch my toes, and twist it to five. When it rang again, going back felt easier, because I knew another break was coming. Four rounds, and my homework was done before the dal reached the table. Ammi would pat that timer like it was a pet.

qa.q: What kind of timer did Ammi buy?
qa.a: A white plastic kitchen timer, the ticking kind.

qa.q: Why did going back to work feel easier for young Varun?
qa.a: He felt less trapped and more willing, because he knew another break was coming soon.

qa.q: Which choice in the story made the plan work?
qa.a: Using the five minutes to move and drink water, so each twenty-minute block started fresh.

qa.q: How did Ammi seem to feel about the timer?
qa.a: She patted it like a pet, so she seemed pleased and fond of how it made homework calmer.

grounding: Shows a child using a kitchen timer for twenty minutes of work and five minutes of water and stretching, finishing homework before dinner.

subtype: Approach: working in short blocks with small breaks [Action]
passage: Anirban had harmonium practice in the next room, and the same wobbly song kept drifting through the wall. Alka had five sums, a science answer and a spelling list, and dinner was at eight. She went to the kitchen, took the old egg timer and set it for twenty minutes. "Work till it rings," she told herself. She did three sums. Ding. Five minutes: a glass of water, arms up to the ceiling, a peek at Anirban, who stuck his tongue out. Then twenty minutes again: two sums and the science answer. Ding. Water, stretch. The last block was spellings. By 7:45 everything was in her bag.

qa.q: What did Alka do during her breaks?
qa.a: She drank a glass of water, stretched her arms up to the ceiling and peeked at Anirban.

qa.q: What do Alka's words 'Work till it rings' suggest about her mood?
qa.a: She seemed determined and focused despite the wobbly harmonium, using the timer to steady herself.

qa.q: What else could Alka try if the noise got worse?
qa.a: Use a break to ask Anirban to close his door, or move to a quieter spot; the short blocks already made the noise easier to bear.

qa.q: What might the evening be like for Anirban?
qa.a: Anirban gets to practise and tease Alka through the doorway, and probably doesn't know how distracting the song was.

grounding: Illustrates a child working in twenty-minute timed blocks with five-minute water and stretch breaks, finishing before dinner despite noise.
